articles.text: With Round 2 in the books, it is time for a quick turnaround as Round 3 of the [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge] already tips off tonight. Here's a quick review of my guard recommendations from Round 2. Carlik Jones had 28.6 fantasy points and Sylvain Francisco finished with 27.5, both turned out as great selections. So was Scottie Wilbekin who had 19.8 points, a great value with his price of 7.7 credits. On the other end of the spectrum, Marc-Owen Fodzo Dada had -1 fantasy points in Round 3, and Dovydas Giedraitis finished with -2. My advice is not limited to guards, also check out my [center] recommendations, and a short list of forwards will be published later today. Here is who I like at guard in Round 3: ### **Scottie Wilbekin, Besiktas Istanbul (8.2 credits)** After playing just seven EuroLeague games in the last two seasons, Wilbekin is back to the player that fans used to love and opponents used to fear. Wilbekin had a great game against one of his former teams, Maccabi, finishing it with 20 points on 4-of-5 three-pointers, three assists and a PIR of 18 in less than 23 minutes. Right now, Wilbekin is a big bargain in the game. ### **Luca Vildoza, Partizan Mozzart Bet Belgrade (8.4 credits)** It has been a while since we last saw a EuroLeague player collect 10 steals in the opening two games of the competition. Despite coming off the bench, Vildoza is really posting solid numbers: 11.5 points on 85.7% three-pointers, 2.5 assists, 5.0 steals and a PIR of 15.0. He plays against FC Bayern Munich in Round 3. Just go for him. ### **Theo Maledon, Real Madrid (10 credits)** It is a bit surprising to see Real at 0-2 right now, and this is exactly why I think *Los Blancos* players should be considered in Round 3. The team faces Hapoel in Sofia, it is a rematch of last season's playoff series, and Maledon has been playing well so far, averaging 10.0 points, 4.0 rebounds, 5.5 assists and 4.5 fouls drawn for a PIR average of 14.0. Players with all-around contributions always pay off. ### **Sterling Brown, Zalgiris Kaunas (10.7 credits)** We spoke about Zalgiris's guard situation before Round 2. Well, Dovydas Giedraitis and Maodo Lo each had a negative PIR, Carsen Edwards had a solid game and Brown was the only player who overperformed. We could expect more or less the same as Zalgiris visits fast-paced Paris in Round 3. He averaged a PIR of 18.5 in two games against Paris last season, better than his season average of 11.0. ### **TJ Shorts, Valencia Basket (15.3 credits)** Valencia set a new all-time scoring club record, getting 111 points against Baskonia, and should keep pushing the pedal against ASVEL. Shorts had 10 assists and just one turnovers in Round 2, getting a PIR of 20 while taking only eight field goal attempts. Going back to France should bring Shorts good memories, and that makes him even more attractive, a top-class choice.

articles.title: EuroLeague Fantasy Tips, Round 3: Centers
articles.text: The 2026-27 [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge] is underway! Need to find a good trade? You got four of them, and I am here to help you with choosing a big man! Here's a quick review of my center picks from Round 2. Mathias Lessort shined with 24.2 points, and Olek Balcerowski had 15 fantasy points, which was a nice value pick since his price was 8.3 credits. Dan Oturu had 9.9 fantasy points, Johannes Voigtmann accumulated 8 points and Kevarrius Hayes was not my best pick, finishing with -0.9 fantasy points. My advice is not limited to big men, these are my [guard] recommendations, and forwards will be published later today. Here is who I like at center in Round 3: ### **Jonas Valanciunas, Zalgiris Kaunas (16 credits)** You may think that Paris's fast-paced game might be too much for a big man like Valanciunas. Well, think again. He has been just unstoppable until now, averaging 12.0 points, 7.0 rebounds, 4.5 assists, 2.0 blocks and a PIR of 22.5. Arvydas Sabonis's last season, 2003-04, was the one before we created the game. Is JV the closest thing to "Sabas" in fantasy? Probably! ### **Mathias Lessort, Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens (15.3 credits)** We don't like to repeat ourselves a lot, but if you don't have Lessort, it is probably bad for your fantasy team. Lessort is on a mission to outpower any other big man out there, and faces Maccabi, a team against he might feel he has something to prove. We know that the former player rule is not written in stone, but Lessort has been on fire lately and should keep going. ### **Marcus Bingham, Fenerbahce Tarfin Istanbul (11.4 credits)** After showing hints of what he was able to do during the Euroleague Basketball SuperCup, Bingham had an excellent EuroLeague debut with Fenerbahce: 12 points on 5-of-7 shooting, 3 rebounds, 1 block and a PIR of 15 in less than 16 minutes. You can expect rebounds, a lot of blocked shots and an occasional three-pointer from now on. At his price, Bingham is a good choice. ### **Tonye Jekiri, Partizan Mozzart Bet Belgrade (9.2 credits)** That center situation in Partizan is hard to figure out but hey, we know this much: Jekiri is a very steady choice with a high floor. He will always get some rebounds, block one or two shots and score with good efficiency. In Paris, Jekiri had 15 points, seven rebounds and a PIR of 22, hitting 7-of-10 two-pointers. Despite Joffrey Lauvergne potentially returning, but Derek Willis still out, we like him. ### **Aliou Diarra, Virtus Bologna (7.2 credits)** EuroLeague Fantasy managers have been complaining to us for two weeks about the lack of cheap, good centers. Well, if that's your thing and you watched the Italian derby in Round 2, now you know one. Diarra finished the game with 15 points on 6-of-9 two-pointers, 7 rebounds, 4 blocks and a PIR of 22. He had a PIR of 10 against Fenerbahce in Round 1. Virtus's next opponent, Olympiacos, is without Nikola Milutinov.

articles.title: EuroLeague Fantasy winners and losers, Round 2: Wednesday
articles.text: - [Tuesday's Fantasy Challenge winners and losers] Just two games took place on Wednesday as Round 2 came to a close, and plenty of [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge] managers were hoping to find a savior, or hoping their opponents didn't. Some smart managers found top performers at a cheap price; others watched their expensive bets flop. Here are Wednesday's Fantasy winners and losers from Round 2's second night. ### Fantasy winners ##### Devon Dotson, Besiktas Istanbul At 9.9 credits entering Round 2, [Devon Dotson] was priced as a mid-tier guard, but boy did he pay off for the 0.5% who had faith in him. He returned 26.4 fantasy points in Besiktas's 93-109 win at Maccabi Rapyd Tel Aviv. Expect his price to rise after this start to life in the EuroLeague. ##### Lefteris Mantzoukas, Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens At this point, it's no longer a surprise. [Lefteris Mantzoukas] would be a prime Breakout Fantasy Star candidate if that award existed. Valued at 4.8 credits entering Round 2, he finished with 20.9 Fantasy points in Panathinaikos's 102-79 win over LDLC ASVEL Villeurbanne. Some 16.1% of you clearly heeded [Frankie and Javi's advice from the podcast]. Well done. ##### Nikos Rogkavopoulos, Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens Mantzoukas got the acclaim, but [Nikos Rogkavopoulos] reminded everyone what he's capable of, finishing with 19.8 Fantasy points in the Greens' beatdown of ASVEL. The 6.1% who owned the 4.4-credit forward, despite him sitting out Round 1, must be feeling good about themselves, especially since I expected Konstantinos Mitoglou to be the one who broke out. ### Fantasy losers ##### Isaac Bonga, Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens You'd expect [Isaac Bonga] to be a consistent fantasy performer at Panathinaikos, but that hasn't been the case: 1.1 points in Round 1, then 3.3 in Round 2. At 11.0 credits, the 5.6% who own him must be weighing whether to jump ship. Bonga's always been a better real-life player than a fantasy one, despite his improvement in fantasy last season, so his value could easily keep sliding. ##### Jae Crowder, LDLC ASVEL Villeurbanne Another pricey forward at 10.2 credits, [Jae Crowder] came back down to earth on Wednesday. After an impressive Round 1 debut, the 5.0% riding that wave got just 6.0 fantasy points as ASVEL fell at Panathinaikos. With a home game against Valencia Basket up next, it's worth watching if he bounces back. ##### Keaton Wallace, Maccabi Rapyd Tel Aviv It's been a tricky start for [Keaton Wallace]. After -3 fantasy points in Round 1, at least 3.0 in Round 2 is progress, but not what you want from a 10.2-credit price tag. As a newbie, he's owned by just 0.6% of managers, and I don't expect that to climb until he finds his feet. There are better options at that cost, or cheaper.

articles.title: EuroLeague Fantasy winners and losers, Round 2: Tuesday
articles.text: Eight of Round 2's 10 games were played on Tuesday night, so the performance of players in those games on your [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge] teams carries a lot of weight. Did you get the low-priced studs to boost your lineup? Did you get burned by high-priced flops? And nearly as important, who did those you compete against have? Let's break down which players sent your heart singing and which ones left you searching for a paper bag to cover your head with. Here are Tuesday’s fantasy winners and losers: ### Fantasy winners ### [Aliou Diarra, Virtus Bologna] What was I thinking! I researched Aliou Diarra. I believed in him. I had him on my roster for Round 1. And then I dropped him. What a fool I was! Diarra erupted for 15 points, 7 rebounds and 4 blocks, amassing a PIR of 22. If you are among the 2.1% of fantasy managers who had him, you got great value for a mere 6.6 credits. He’ll be more expensive by Round 3. ### [Dylan Osetkowski, Valencia Basket] A PIR of 20 is certainly not unheard of for Dylan Osetkowski, but it’s not common either. He had reached that number 4 times in 62 EuroLeague appearances entering this week. And then on Tuesday he scored 12 points on near-perfect shooting for a PIR of 20 off the bench in a blowout win over Baskonia. A fantastic performance for a 7.7-credit player. ### [Luca Vildoza, Partizan Mozzart Bet Belgrade] With a line of 16 points and 6 steals, Luca Vildoza defied logic to help Partizan win in Paris. He earned 23.1 fantasy points for the 5.3% of owners bold enough to pay the 7.8-credit price tag on the Argentinian guard. It was the first time in 15 games that Vildoza had achieved a PIR of at least 20. How long until he does it again with Partizan? ### Fantasy losers ### [Timothe Luwawu-Cabarrot, Real Madrid] There is no way around it. If you were among the 5.4% of fantasy owners to roster Timothe Luwawu-Cabarrot this week, you are in a bad place. It’s a trifecta of doom. His negative-10 PIR dooms your team this week. The fact that it came from a player you paid 12.4 credits for adds salt to the wound. And the relatively high loss in credits (it could be as high as a full credit!) you will see factored into TLC’s price before Round 3 dooms you a second time. Yikes! ### [Dario Brizuela, FC Barcelona] Oh, the fantasy gods can be so fickle! A week ago, we were celebrating those who had the foresight to pay 6.4 credits for Dario Brizuela as he racked up 17.6 fantasy points for just 6.4 credits. His price even rose 0.4 credits. Did you then sell him? Few did. Brizuela is owned by 8.9% of managers in Round 2 and he did not reward them. The Basque Mamba was held scoreless and posted a PIR of negative-8. Another tough pill to swallow. ### [Tyrique Jones, Olympiacos Piraeus] Sometimes fantasy owners (myself included) are naïve enough to think that when a star is sidelined, someone else can step into his minutes and perform. And sometimes we strike gold. Other times, we see Tyrique Jones give us 1.1 fantasy points after we paid 12.1 credits hoping he would dominate with Nikola Milutinov out. I say “we” to be kind. I didn’t make this mistake. But 2.2% of owners did. Better luck next time, my friends.

articles.title: EuroLeague Fantasy Round 2: Who to hold, buy, or sell
articles.text: The Round 1 of EuroLeague Fantasy is behind us, but after just one round, it is difficult to draw any definitive conclusions about players. A player’s performance and value can change significantly from round to round, so it is important to look at the bigger picture, including form, minutes, role within the team, and the upcoming schedule. That is why in this feature we will track EuroLeague players across the HOLD, BUY and SELL categories: players worth keeping, players whose value could rise, and players for whom it may be the right time to make a change. EuroLeague Fantasy Prices 2026-27: All 326 Player Credits HOLD Moses Wright – Milano – 13.7 credits Milano arguably boast the most favorable upcoming schedule in the entire EuroLeague. Over the next stretch, they will lock horns with Virtus, Baskonia, and Maccabi Tel Aviv – matchups where their frontcourt should flourish. While Moses Wright was completely contained in the opening round against Partizan and finished with a single-digit fantasy score, one quiet game does not alter his long-term outlook. He remains the central focal point around whom Milano’s tactical system will revolve this season. A massive number of fantasy managers placed their trust in him for Round 1, and selling him now would be premature. He is a primary hold for Round 2. Joel Parra – Barcelona – 6.7 credits Selected by roughly 30% of fantasy managers in the opening round, Joel Parra delivered a massive disappointment by finishing with zero fantasy points and suffering a 0.3 credit price drop. However, dropping him immediately based on a single outlier would be a mistake. Parra remains the premier budget option in his price range, slotted into a vital role as one of Barcelona’s primary anchors. Outside of that Round 1 bump, he consistently posted index ratings above 20 throughout preseason and Liga Endesa . His role and talent remain intact – hold him for Round 2 and expect a swift rebound. Arijan Lakic – Partizan – 4.0 credits Arijan Lakic is an absolute must-have asset at his minimum 4.0-credit valuation. Securing a baseline role of around 20 minutes per game at the basement price tier offers unparalleled roster flexibility. With Derek Willis sidelined, Partizan’s already depleted rotation shrinks even further, locking in Lakic’s court time and usage. His price tag is heavily insulated with massive upward mobility, making him a prime candidate to appreciate in market value. Holding him is a no-brainer until he approaches the 4.5 to 4.8 credit threshold – until then, keep him firmly locked in your lineup. EuroLeague Fantasy Round 2 Tips: Best Player Picks & Head Coaches BUY T.J. Shorts – Valencia – 15.1 credits Alongside Milano, Valencia hand managers one of the most enticing fixture runs over the next two rounds, locking horns with Baskonia at home before traveling to face Asvel. The up tempo, high-possessions game state expected in both encounters fits T.J. Shorts ’ game like a glove. If you passed on him in Round 1, bringing him in now is essential. He immediately demonstrated that Valencia is his team, taking full ownership as the focal offensive leader and engine. Expecting him to comfortably eclipse 20 fantasy points across both matchups is a realistic baseline given his dominant, high-usage workload. Dinos Mitoglou – Panathinaikos – 5.9 credits With Juancho Hernangomez questionable for the upcoming double round due to a groin issue, Panathinaikos’ already tight rotation upfront gets even thinner. That leaves head coach Zeljko Obradovic relying heavily on a frontcourt core of Mathias Lessort , Guerschon Yabusele , and Dinos Mitoglou . At a budget price tag of just 5.9 credits, Mitoglou represents extraordinary value. He is in line for an expanded role with a clear path to 20+ minutes of playing time while Panathinaikos navigate a highly favorable stretch of games. Given his scoring and rebounding potential, he is one of the top low-cost BUY targets on the market for Round 2. Mario Saint-Supery – Valencia – 4.9 credits Mario Saint-Supery stands out as another compelling Valencia player to target on the fantasy wire. Early rotation trends confirm that the young Spanish guard is firmly entrenched in the rotation, commanding a reliable 15 to 20 minutes of action per night. His affordable 4.9-credit price tag lowers the risk threshold significantly while delivering strong returns on minimal investment. Operating within an uptempo offense, he presents an ideal budget-enabler to anchor the end of your bench and free up critical capital for elite producers elsewhere. Buy him now before his valuation climbs. EuroLeague Fantasy Preview: Players Who Produce Well but Aren’t Fantasy Options SELL Jonas Valanciunas – Zalgiris – 15.9 credits Jonas Valanciunas was a dominant force against Crvena Zvezda in Round 1, imposing his will across the court to rack up a massive 26.4 fantasy points. Despite that explosive debut, selling him now is the smartest strategic move. Early signs suggest he experienced stamina fatigue early in that contest, raising valid durability concerns. With Zalgiris preparing to navigate demanding fixtures against fast-paced teams like Olympiacos and Paris, Valanciunas may struggle to match their relentless tempo. Moving on from him for the upcoming stretch allows you to reallocate premium capital into more sustainable, uptempo assets before reassessing his status later. Joel Bolomboy – Asvel – 10.2 credits Joel Bolomboy proved to be a major disappointment for fantasy managers in the opening round. Despite logging 26 minutes of action against Maccabi Tel Aviv, he remained virtually invisible on the offensive end, attempting a total of just two field goals throughout the contest. Early tactical signs indicate that he sits at the bottom of Asvel’s offensive hierarchy. Factor in a daunting road trip to face Panathinaikos in Round 2, and the writing is on the wall: now is the time to sell. Asvel’s fixture list eases up down the line, so if his offensive involvement picks up, he may re-emerge as a viable budget target later in the season. Bruno Fernando – Anadolu Efes – 10.0 credits Much like Joel Bolomboy, Bruno Fernando proved to be a major disappointment for fantasy managers in the opening round. He managed to scrape together just 3 fantasy points despite facing a shorthanded Barcelona frontcourt. With Anadolu Efes bracing for an exceptionally difficult schedule in the upcoming stretch, holding onto a center with low usage and minimal court time is an unnecessary liability. Fernando should be removed from your fantasy roster without second thought and replaced with higher-floor, more dependable options in his price tier. articles.title: EuroLeague Fantasy Tips, Round 2: Centers
articles.text: The 2026-27 [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge] has just started! Not off to a good start? Don't worry, I am here to help you! You have four trades, so let's use them wisely. This may be the help you need to bounce back! Here's a quick review of my center picks from Round 1. Jonas Valanciunas was a slam dunk as he marked his return to the EuroLeague with 26.4 fantasy points and a gain of 0.4 credits. Kevarrius Hayes was also a clever pick as he went for 13.2 fantasy points and gained 0.2 credits, while Allan Dokossi was nearly as good with 12 fantasy points and a gain of 0.1 credits. Moses Wright hurt a lot of us with just 9 fantasy points, which caused him to lose 0.3 credits and I was too high on Austin Wiley, who ran into foul trouble, scored just 4.4 fantasy points and lost 0.3 credits. My advice is not limited to big men. Go see my [guard] and [forward] recommendations. Here is who I like at center in Round 2: ### Mathias Lessort, Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens (15.0 credits) It is a very simple decision to make: if you have the credits, you should go for [Mathias Lessort]. First, he is a T2 player, so if Vezen... if your captain doesn't play well, then you have a great choice with a very high floor. Lessort was at his very best in Round 1 with 15 points, 9 rebounds, 3 blocks and 9 fouls drawn against Paris. Who will stop him from now on? ### Dan Oturu, Hapoel Tel Aviv (14.9 credits) [Dan Oturu] had an outstanding first quarter against Bayern with 9 points and 8 rebounds. He looked on his way to be MVP of the Round, but slowed down and Hapoel didn't win. He finished that game with huge numbers: 20 points on 10-of-11 two-point shooting, 12 rebounds and 2 blocks for a PIR of 32. Oturu is Coach Itoudis's number one choice at center. He should be on your team. ### Olek Balcerowski, FC Barcelona (8.3 credits) If you need a cheaper option, then you can go for [Olek Balcerowski], who had a couple of really good performances last week. He opened the EuroLeague season with a bang: 10 points and 4 rebounds for a PIR of 14 against Efes. Balcerowski did even better in the Spanish League with 21 points and 6 rebounds for a PIR of 30. Josh Nebo is out, so it's Balcerowski's time in fantasy. ### Johannes Voigtmann, FC Bayern Munich (7.9 credits) Yes, Bayern plays against Fenerbahce, but it comes off a big win against Hapoel on [Johannes Voigtmann]'s go-ahead three-pointer. He made the most of his 19 minutes on the floor with 10 points, 5 rebounds and 3 assists for a PIR of 17, while making few mistakes. Voigtmann has a lot of talent and experience, and comes off a game-winning shot. At his price, he is a good option. ### Kevarrius Hayes, Partizan Mozzart Bet Belgrade (7.5 credits) Last week, we talked about Partizan centers and how they would split minutes. Well, with Joffrey Lauvergne sidelined, [Kevarrius Hayes] and Tonye Jekiri are seeing more playing time and making the most of it. Hayes started in Round 1, finishing the game against Milan with 10 points on 5-of-6 shooting and 3 rebounds for a PIR of 12. Definitely not bad for 7.5 credits, right?

articles.title: EuroLeague Fantasy Tips, Round 2: Forwards
articles.text: The 2026-27 EuroLeague is underway and so is the [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge]. I know, Round 1 left some disappointments but now, you have four trades to improve your team. Even better, I are here to help you with some fantasy tips. MY picks at forward were disappointing for me too. Though I did well to recommend Eleftherios Mantzoukas of Panathinaikos, that's where the success ended. Mantzoukas scored 13.2 fantasy points and gained 0.3 credits. Timothe Luwawu-Cabarrot (5 fantasy points, lost 0.4 credits), Joel Parra (0 fantasy points, lost 0.3 credits) and Jordan Nwora (8 fantasy points, lost 0.2 credits) all hurt their owners and the only reasons that Stefan Joksimovic (-1 fantasy points) didn’t lose credits is because he started at the minimum price. Yikes! I am determined to do better in all my picks this time. My recommendations at [guard] and [center] are already live and here are five forwards for the future for all budgets. ### Dario Saric, Anadolu Efes Istanbul (14.9 credits) That is the way you come back to the EuroLeague, with a huge game and leaving no doubt about your ability. [Dario Saric] had a strong Round 1 game against Barca with 17 points on 8-of-9 free throw shooting, 5 rebounds and 7 fouls drawn for a PIR of 26. He was also great in his team's Turkish League opener with 16 points and a PIR of 25. Real is up next, so expect him to keep leading Efes. ### Azuolas Tubelis, Zalgiris Kaunas (11.6 credits) Frankie Sachs always talks about sensational sophomores in the EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge podcast. [Azuolas Tubelis] had an outstanding first season and is determined to do even better now. He proved it in Round 1 against Zvezda with 10 points, 12 rebounds, 4 assists and a PIR of 23. At just 11.6 credits, Tubelis is a great opportunity for all fantasy managers out there. ### Tadas Sedekerskis, Baskonia Vitoria-Gasteiz (10.5 credits) After an injury-plagued year, [Tadas Sedekerskis] is back and seems to be in good shape, too. articles.title: EuroLeague Fantasy Tips, Round 2: Guards
articles.text: Round 1 of the 2026-27 EuroLeague seasons is in the books and with it the first round of the [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge], too. Now we are heading into the first double-round week of the season. It is time to check the schedule, look for Turn 2 players who will deliver in Round 2, and reload your rosters before the next deadline, on Tuesday at 18:00 CET. My Round 1 picks were pretty good and three of them gained 0.2 credits! They were, TJ Shorts, who scored 22 fantasy points, Nigel Williams-Goss with 15.4 points and young Mario Saint-Supery with 11 fantasy points. Meanwhile Sylvain Francisco had 19.8 fantasy points and went up 0.1 credits. Alas, Matteo Spagnolo accounted for 7 fantasy points and his price remained the same. Here are five guards who deserve serious consideration for Round 2. I have made my picks at [forward] and [center], too. ### Sylvain Francisco, Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens (14.9 credits) I said we would focus on T2 players, which means there will be a lot of Panathinaikos players in all fantasy articles this week. Panathinaikos is the heavy favorite to win both games at Telekom Center Athens. [Sylvain Francisco] signed for ASVEL early in the off-season and ended up playing for Panathinaikos. It should be a special game for him, so keep an eye on him. ### Carlik Jones, Partizan Mozzart Bet Belgrade (14.5 credits) This is almost a no-brainer. [Carlik Jones] was the Round 1 MVP and even though Partizan plays twice on the road this week, it faces fast-paced teams in Paris and Bayern. He should keep leading Partizan the way he did in Round 1, making Jones a must for all fantasy teams. If you got him in Round 1, don't sell him. If you missed him, he is still affordable, so go for it. ### Scottie Wilbekin, Besiktas Istanbul (7.7 credits) In recent years, [Scottie Wilbekin] may not have been the best fantasy player, but at 7.7 credits, it is hard to ignore a player of his caliber. He had a solid Round 1 game against Valencia, getting a PIR of 13, and goes against Maccabi in Round 2. Wilbekin remains Maccabi's all-time top scorer in the EuroLeague with 1,801 points. Talent and motivation always go well together! ### Marc-Owen Fodzo Dada, LDLC ASVEL Villeurbanne (5.3 credits) This is a surprise that few saw coming. [Marc-Owen Fodzo Dada] took over in Round 1, leading ASVEL to an 84-74 home win over Maccabi with 14 points, 5 assists and a PIR of 17 as a starter, playing over 21 minutes. An isolated good game? Think again. Fodzo Dada also played almost 21 minutes in French League action, too. All aboard the Fodzo Dada train! ### Dovydas Giedraitis, Zalgiris Kaunas (4.3 credits) Owned by just 1.3% of fantasy managers at the moment, [Dovydas Giedraitis] is a very cheap option that should allow you to afford other players. [Nigel Williams-Goss] is sidelined for Zalgiris, which opens the door for Giedraitis, who started and played 20 minutes in the Lithuanian League on Sunday. Giedraitis is a cheap get for all fantasy managers.

articles.title: EuroLeague Fantasy Tips Round 2 & 3
articles.text: As I always did, I’m just going to ignore some of the obvious expensive options like Sasa Vezenkov, Jonas Valanciunas, Sylvain Francisco, Mike James, etc. Round 2 has a particularity, cause only 4 teams will have their matchup in Turn 2, so that means we have to think about players to captain in those 4 teams, to be able to have a decent captain in both turns. I always like to include those players who are not that obvious or if they are, at least in the moment I recommend them is one of the best moments of the season, based on matchup streak, current shape, etc. I also tend to not repeat the ones I recommended last round, so take all this into account. 🧠GUARDS Chris Jones (12.6 cr): On the roster analysis for Zvezda I already talked about him possibly nearing his prime on this Zvezda, and I was not far from the truth. He has started the season in a really great way, showing leadership as playmaker, but also confience on the scoring side. He might not be the one with the biggest usage, but I think that will increase gradually. Theo Maledon (10 cr): We predicted Theo being one of the players taking a step forward with Pedro Martínez and that’s what we’ve seen until now. He did an amazing preseason, now he has started the season in an unbeatable way, being the best player in both games played so far (EL & ACB). Devon Hall (8.5 cr): We’ve already seen the usage coach Poetta will give him, so that added to his capacity to contribute from every aspect of the game, makes him a great option. He might not be the best scorer, but I think he’s a pretty safe player, as he probably won’t get a -5 FPTS game. Maodo Lo (7.1 cr): After finding out the 2-weeks injury of Nigel Williams-Goss, the first direct replacement that comes to my mind is Maodo Lo, who should be the one to get his minutes. He might not be on his best career moment, but he has the quality and talent to put up a really great performance as playmaker. Marc-Owen Fodzo Dada (5.3 cr): He seemed to have a really quick adaptation to top-level basketball and a pretty decent usage to be that young, so it looks like a great option on that price. He’ll play in Turn 2, so that makes it even better as a Round 2 choice, even though teammates like Patty Mills could be the musts. 🎯FORWARDS Kameron Taylor (12.6 cr): His last season was really good, but he started this one even better, so I think on a team where he might be one of the scoring references during all the season and with his rebounding capacity, the ceiling is really far from where he’s right now. Alec Peters (12 cr): While Garrison Mathews remains sidelined, he might be one of the best Forwards available in Fantasy terms. His playing time is already pretty high (30 mins) and will keep being like this as long as Mathews is injured. He just need to contribute a little bit more in rebounding and defensively to become the ultimate choice. Kessler Edwards (10 cr): He’s a really complete PF that already got a massive performance on this season Italian Supercup vs Milano (25 EFF). He can get +10 FPTS without even scoring, so imagine the potential if he gets a great game in terms of scoring, on a game that will be easier for him than Fener. Dinos Mitoglou (5.9 cr): He started the season in a really great shape, with the confidence he was missing last season, so being that cheap and while NHD keeps sidelined, he could have really great performances as he’s good on rebounding, but also on mid-range and 3pt shooting. 🗼CENTERS Mathias Lessort (15 cr): He’s an obvious choice, but especially this round against ASVEL and being probably the best captain option for Round 2, Turn 2. He seems to be again nearing his prime and that means the ceiling of this guy is still really far from 15 credits, so it might be time to select him. O. Balcerowski (8.3 cr) : As Nebo keeps sidelined, he’s performing on surprising numbers in both EuroLeague & ACB first games, so he might be one of the best mid-price centers right now. Great rebounding capacity and accompanied by pretty good playmakers in terms of creating spaces for him to end up alone under the basket. Jasiel Rivero (7.5 cr): Two great rounds ahead for Valencia facing 2 of the “weakest” teams on paper and especially Baskonia being a really bad frontcourt defender. That makes Jasiel a really good option to consider in cheap options, as he could be in advantage under the basket quite a lot of times. Thanks for reading EuroBallin' Substack! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.

articles.title: EuroLeague Fantasy winners and losers, Round 1: Thursday
articles.text: Opening night of the 2026-27 EuroLeague season is in the books and Thursday's slate of games already delivered its share of heroes and heartbreak – especially for [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge] managers. Whether you're basking in the glow of a breakout performance from a value pick or nursing the wounds of a big-money bust who no-showed, every fantasy manager has a story to tell after night one. Let's break down which players padded your scoreline and which ones left you searching for the bench button. Here are Thursday’s fantasy winners and losers: ### Fantasy winners #### [Tyler Dorsey, Olympiacos Piraeus] Last season, Dorsey scored at least 20 points in his first two games. He started strong again this season with 25 points on excellent shooting to finish with 31.9 fantasy points. Though Dorsey is not a cheap player, coming in at 12.6 credits, he provided plenty of value to the 3.5% of owners who signed him for Round 1. #### [Marc-Owen Fodzo Dada, LDLC ASVEL Villeurbanne] Still a teenager, Fodzo Dada posted a manly performance for ASVEL at home with 14 points and 5 assists for 18.7 fantasy points, which cost a mere 4.8 credits! I recommended him on the [EuroLeague Fantasy Challenge Podcast], but what can I do that only 1.1% of owners took my advice? I am pretty sure that number will rise this week, but you will be buying him at a higher price. #### [Azuolas Tubelis, Zalgiris Kaunas] While all the attention was on his frontcourt mate [Jonas Valanciunas], Tubelis was almost as productive, but at a significant discount. The Zalgiris power forward posted 10 points and a career-high 12 rebounds, recording his second EuroLeague double-double, while totaling 25.3 fantasy points. That’s quite a haul for his 11.1-credit price tag. Tubelis was owned by 6.5% of fantasy owners, and those managers were winners on Thursday, too. ### Fantasy losers #### [Johnathan Motley, Crvena Zvezda Meridianbet Belgrade] Center is not always an easy fantasy position. And if you were among the 2.5% of fantasy owners who had Motley in your lineup, it became a nightmare position for you on Thursday. One in 40 fantasy teams spent 11.0 credits on a center who recorded minus-13 fantasy points. Ouch! Even though in almost all cases Motley will wind up on the fantasy bench (every owner who has a pulse and a phone will bench him on Friday), which will mitigate the damage, this performance will also result in lost credits. Ouch again! #### [Nikola Milutinov, Olympiacos Piraeus] I don’t know why, but 2.6% of fantasy owners had Milutinov this week despite the injury concerns. In the end, he played 9 minutes off the bench and scored 3.3 fantasy points. His owners paid 15.3 credits for that. Milutinov was the sixth-highest priced player in the game and will be among the lowest-scoring fantasy players in Round 1. From a credit standpoint, it would have been better for his owners had Milutinov not played at all. #### [Joel Parra, FC Barcelona] This one hurt a lot of fantasy players because Parra is the second-most-owned player in Round 1 at a whopping 30.9%! Parra started and played nearly 27 minutes, which is great for a player who cost 7.0 credits. However, on Thursday he shot poorly, missing 8 of the 10 shots he took. That left him with a fantasy score of 0. Well, at least his owners have plenty of company.

articles.text: Euroleague Basketball is pleased to announce the introduction of a new referee nomination system that will determine referee crews for each round of both the EuroLeague and BKT EuroCup. digest.summary_el:
• Ξεκινά η 3η αγωνιστική της EuroLeague με διπλή αγωνιστική εβδομάδα.
• Ο Σίλβειν Φρανσίσκο και ο Τι Τζέι Σορτς συνεχίζουν να αποτελούν κορυφαίες επιλογές στα γκαρντ.
• Ο Ματίας Λεσόρ προτείνεται ως κορυφαία επιλογή για αρχηγός (captain) στο φάνταζι.
• Σημαντικές απουσίες όπως του Νίκολα Μιλουτίνοφ για τον Ολυμπιακό και του Χουάντσο Ερνανγκόμεθ για τον Παναθηναϊκό.
• Παίκτες όπως ο Λευτέρης Μαντζούκας και ο Αλιού Ντιαρά προσφέρουν εξαιρετική αξία σε χαμηλές τιμές.
• Η Βιλερμπάν τιμωρήθηκε με απαγόρευση μεταγραφών λόγω οφειλών στον Τζόφρι Λοβέρν.
• Η Μακάμπι Τελ Αβίβ ψάχνει αντίδραση μετά το αρνητικό ξεκίνημα και την ήττα από την Μπεσίκτας.
